items.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021
items.q: But he lived right across the street from Striker’s where I was playing a couple of nights with Chet Baker and then I started playing a couple of nights with Lee.

ctx.x: What do you consider in the 70s going into the 80s as really important musical associations for yourself, playing gigs and recording perhaps?

Well definitely when I, you know my Chet Baker association, which went to about 1976 or so, and then during that time I also met Lee Konitz and started playing with him. There was a place called Striker’s Pub on West 86th Street. So I met Lee Konitz and that was very influential. I had actually met Lee Konitz initially at Saul Fromkin’s where he was a customer of Saul Fromkin but that was not, I met him as a woodwind repairman but then I met him later on and actually in the park walking our dogs because we were…

items.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That was one of the few times I felt like I had some kind of a band and appreciated that.

ctx.x: But you did a lot of nice records with Harold and a number of gigs both here and in Europe right?
